pr_body:
Modules that aren't activated at conf load time don't seem to set the module path from the template leading to load failures.  Make sure to set that

Fixes #24020
pr_comments: Should there be some test for this?

> Should there be some test for this?

+1
test added to ensure modulepath works

Its very much relevant, yes.  I thought it would be quick to add the tests, but specifying a module path for a module comes with various restrictions about being able to run the test only when the right extension is applied to the module and when its actually built (i.e. can't run the test for windows/macosx, as the modulepath can't point to p_test.so, as its name is actually p_test.ld/p_test.dylib), nor can I run it when the provider isn't configured to be built.  Fixing now

@nhorman 
I wanted to make a patch out of this change for myself, but I noticed a small bug here:
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/105ecc518ddc8cf7b7fbaa12d631683dcf2bf0c4/crypto/provider_core.c#L575-L585
I think you need to set path **after** null check in line 584, not before it.
This pull request is ready to merge
Merged to the master, 3.3 and 3.2 branches. This does not apply cleanly to 3.1 and 3.0, please open a new PR against 3.1.

issue_context.title: Cannot lazy load providers specified in configuration file correctly
comments:
FWIW, The activate setting has changed somewhat between 3.0 and the head of the tree (and in 3.3).  In 3.0 the activate setting was an implied boolean whos presence meant activate if it was present (i.e. you could set activate=no and that would still activate the provider).  In 3.3 it was updated such that activate was a positively asserted boolean (i.e. activate=[1|yes|true] means activate, 0|no|false means don't activate.  Omitting the parameter is an error.  you might need to check that.

But I don't think thats whats going on here.  I think whats happening is that we're expressly forgetting to set the path when creating a provider.  When we call provider_conf_load, if its not going to be activated, we create a template in which we do wet the path in the OSSL_PROVIDER_INFO struct, but unlike the activate path we don't call ossl_provider_set_module_path (which makes sense, as we don't have an OSSL_PROVIDER struct yet).  However, in the provider_new call which we make during a manual call to OSSL_PROVIDER_load, we get the template, but we never set the allocated provider path with a call to ossl_provider_set_module_path.  I think we probably need to.  Can you augment thee ossl_provider_new code to add a call to that function prior to the call to provider_new call there passing the value of template.path as the argument?
Can you attempt to run your reproducer with the referenced PR and see if the problem is fixed please?

@nhorman 
Hi

I have tested this PR and it works well. It loads provider as expected.
Will this PR be merged into 3.0 branch as well?
Thank you, I've marked it for inclusion in all the 3.x branches.  It will take.a.bit though as we're about to freeze for the final 3.3 release

> Omitting the parameter is an error. you might need to check that.

@nhorman I would strongly disagree with that. Omitting the parameter completely must be supported for backwards compatibility and the default value must be not to activate.
Yeah, you're right, omitting the parameter still defaults to don't activate, which is correct.  It's adding the parameter key without a value that generates.ab error

review_comments: Can `template.path` ever be NULL?  If so, shouldn't you check for it to be non-NULL?

It can.  The NULL check is already handled inside ossl_provider_set_module_path.  If the path is NULL, ossl_provider_set_module_path returns success without actually duplicating the path, which seems correct to me.

Er, it actually does a bit more than that, it *clears* any previously set path.  Is that what you want?

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/e1fd043ad7fa865a8ef9160c892b49a098d23c71/crypto/provider_core.c#L758-L767
I believe so, yes, given that we're adding a call to ossl_provider_set_module_path with a freshly allocated provider returned from provider_new, which never sets the path value at all.
